results.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
results.content: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

results.title: The Gambia election: Can Barrow secure a third term?
results.content: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.

results.title: On the arrest of Informer TV owner and editor-in-chief Dragan J. Vucicevic: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
results.content: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable or whether this is another political power struggle.

results.title: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?
results.content: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could also determine the political fortunes of one of the Philippines' most powerful dynasties.

results.title: Risks of child marriage in Iran complicated by war
results.content: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates warn.

results.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
results.content: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

results.title: Albania's youth are protesting in Flamingo Revolution, not leaving the country anymore
results.content: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

results.title: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?
results.content: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's music scene has evolved hugely thanks to state funding and support. Local musicians and DJs are optimistic. But are they actually just helping prop up an authoritarian state?

results.title: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
results.content: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings.

results.title: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?
results.content: Vietnam has voted to abolish the death penalty for six more crimes, continuing a decades-long trend of restricting capital punishment.

results.title: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
results.content: Opposition politicians and government critics say arrests, prosecutions and restrictions on public activity are making it harder to challenge those in power. Is a broader pattern emerging?
